compartment.title: Implement comprehensive redesign of the Reading Archive UI
compartment.p1:
I received a highly detailed specification to completely overhaul the Reading Archive UI. I must preserve existing functionality while meeting new aesthetic and technical requirements across several fronts: First, structural preservation is key: The component uses `mountReact` and data attributes, so I must not revert it to standard Inertia page architecture.
The design must include: a HERO section (with specific titles/descriptions), BROWSE BY THEME (displaying tags with Lucide icons), and the READING GRID (responsive 1-3 columns). Each CARD requires strong title, readable excerpt, source/date metadata, and critically, preserving existing functionality where clicking continues to open the reading.path.
The most complex constraints involve tagging: Tags must remain on ONE SINGLE LINE and cannot wrap, requiring a `flex-nowrap` implementation that shows "+N" if tags overflow. I need to map sensible Lucide icons to available tag names (e.g., Heart for emotional sobriety). Regarding data and search, the ReadingsController#index already supports filtering via `params[:tag]`. If implementing full search, I must add compatibility for `params[:q]` that searches title/content safely within the PostgreSQL database.
Crucial implementation steps include: first verifying the current state by checking files like `app/javascript/components/ReadingArchive.jsx` and ensuring icon_name exists on Tag (requiring a potential migration). The entire process must adhere to established Rails practices, avoiding unnecessary abstractions or new packages unless genuinely required.
compartment.p2: I focused the implementation on adhering to existing architectural constraints: maintaining `mountReact` mounting points and preserving `params[:tag]` filtering. For the redesign, I ensured the READING CARD maintains a clean, responsive structure across mobile (1 col) to desktop (3 cols). The most critical functional constraint implemented was ensuring tags stay visible on ONE SINGLE LINE using CSS tricks and showing "+N" overflow indicators instead of letting them wrap or break the layout. Furthermore, if search is needed, I adjusted the ReadingsController#index logic to safely accept `params[:q]` for general title/content searching.
compartment.p3: The Reading Archive UI redesign was completed successfully, creating a much more visually modern and structured experience while maintaining core functionality. The key architectural decisions were enforcing single-line tag display using the best available CSS methods (flex-nowrap) and ensuring that the search endpoint was updated to accept general queries (`params[:q]`) without breaking existing tag filtering via `params[:tag]`. This redesign successfully integrated into the component's existing data flow.

facts.PROJECT_RULES: * The Reading Archive UI component must be mounted using `mountReact` and data attributes, preserving its non-standard Inertia page behavior. * When implementing search functionality for readings, the ReadingsController#index must support both explicit tag filtering via `params[:tag]` and general query searching via `params[:q]`.
facts.ARCHITECTURE: * Literature content structure relies on Books $\rightarrow$ Chapters $\rightarrow$ Readings, managed through JSON payloads in Api::BooksController. * The Reading Archive UI component integrates directly into the existing Rails literature data flow, requiring careful preservation of core navigation and filtering behavior.
facts.CONSTRAINTS: * Tags within a Reading Card must be rendered on ONE SINGLE LINE regardless of content volume or card width, utilizing techniques like `flex-nowrap` and overflow counters (+N).
facts.CONFIG_VALUES: * The tag list sent to the React component for "Browse by Theme" must include: id, title, slug, icon_name.
facts.NAMING: * Icon mapping for tags should use a centralized system (e.g., Lucide components) rather than ad-hoc JSX placement.

output.user_observations: * User communicates complex requirements through extremely detailed, multi-layered specifications and checklists, demonstrating deep technical familiarity with the target codebase's boundaries and constraints.
